answer: Prompt architecture, concept art, vector assets, inpainting and colour: the still image made with diffusion models.

children.name: Prompt Architecture and Style Replication
children.blurb: Prompt architecture is the structured design of text and parameter inputs that steer a generative image model toward a specific visual outcome.

children.name: Concept Art and World-Building
children.blurb: Concept art and world-building in generative illustration covers early visual exploration of characters, environments, props, and cultures for games, film, animation, and interactive media.

children.name: Vector Graphics and Interface Assets
children.blurb: Vector graphics and interface assets cover anything drawn as paths, curves, strokes and fills rather than pixels: icons, logos, pictograms, diagrams, maps, type, and the illustration and component art that sits inside a product interface.

children.name: Inpainting and Canvas Expansion
children.blurb: Inpainting is the process of filling a masked or missing region of an image with generated content that matches its surroundings.

children.name: Algorithmic Colour Grading
children.blurb: Algorithmic colour grading covers the use of software algorithms, including machine learning models, to adjust colour, contrast, tone, and look across still images and moving pictures.

sections.body: This section covers the still image as made with diffusion models, from the first text prompt to the final graded frame. In practice, artists use these systems to generate concept sketches, background plates, character designs, icon sets and colour treatments, then refine them by hand or with further model passes. The work is less about a single magic prompt and more about iteration: generate, select, mask, repaint, repeat. Prompt architecture has become a craft of its own, with artists building reusable prompt templates and style references rather than typing one-off sentences. Diffusion models are now a standard tool in illustration pipelines alongside drawing tablets and vector editors, not a replacement for them.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Text to image generation is largely solved for single, well-lit subjects and common styles, and it is reliable enough for mood boards, thumbnails and rough comps. It remains weak at precise spatial control, consistent characters across many images, readable text inside images, and exact colour matching to a brand palette. Inpainting and canvas expansion work well for small edits but degrade when the new region must match complex lighting or perspective. Vector output is still mostly a tracing or conversion step, since diffusion models produce pixels, not clean paths. The legal picture is unsettled: this site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits, and the outcome of those cases will shape what training data and outputs are permissible, though nothing here is legal advice.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run roughly in the order a real project moves. Prompt Architecture and Style Replication is the entry point, covering how prompts are structured and how a look is held steady across a set. Concept Art and World-Building takes that further into environments, characters and props, where consistency across many images matters most. Vector Graphics and Interface Assets handles the conversion problem, turning raster generations into clean paths for icons, logos and UI elements. Inpainting and Canvas Expansion is the repair and extension bench, for fixing hands, removing objects or growing a canvas beyond its original frame. Algorithmic Colour Grading closes the loop, covering palette control, LUT-style transformations and the colour decisions that make a generated image feel finished rather than raw.
